```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(SigBridgeR)
library(Seurat)
```

# Overview

Accuracy alone does not show **which biology** a screening method recovers.
`BenchGSEA()` complements `BenchAcc()` by asking whether the cells selected by
each method are enriched for the pathways that are expected to drive the
phenotype.

For every screening method found in the object, `BenchGSEA()`:

1. binarises the method labels into `"Positive"` and `"Other"`;
2. finds markers between the two groups with `Seurat::FindMarkers()`;
3. ranks the markers by `sign(avg_log2FC) * -log10(p_val_adj)`;
4. runs `fgsea::fgsea()` on the ranked list;
5. records the ranking statistics of the leading-edge genes.

The results of all methods are stacked into one `data.table`, so pathways can
be compared side by side.

# A small example

The following toy dataset contains three pathways. The cells selected by
`Scissor` have extra expression in the first pathway, while the cells selected
by `scPAS` have extra expression in the second pathway. A good benchmark should
therefore recover the matching pathway for each method.

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-data
set.seed(123)

n_genes <- 60L
n_cells <- 18L
gene_names <- paste0("Gene", seq_len(n_genes))
cell_names <- paste0("Cell", seq_len(n_cells))

counts <- matrix(
  rpois(n_genes * n_cells, lambda = 5),
  nrow = n_genes,
  dimnames = list(gene_names, cell_names)
)

scissor_label <- rep(
  c("Positive", "Positive", "Negative", "Other", "Negative", "Other"),
  times = 3L
)
scpas_label <- rep(
  c("Negative", "Other", "Positive", "Positive", "Other", "Negative"),
  times = 3L
)
truth <- rep(c("Positive", "Negative", "Other"), each = 6L)

# * pathway A is active in Scissor-positive cells
counts[1:10, scissor_label == "Positive"] <-
  counts[1:10, scissor_label == "Positive"] + 40L

# * pathway B is active in scPAS-positive cells
counts[11:20, scpas_label == "Positive"] <-
  counts[11:20, scpas_label == "Positive"] + 40L

counts <- Matrix::Matrix(counts, sparse = TRUE)

sc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
sc <- NormalizeData(sc, verbose = FALSE)
sc$truth <- truth
sc$Scissor <- scissor_label
sc$scPAS <- scpas_label
```

`pathways` is a named list of gene sets, exactly as expected by `fgsea()`:

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-pathways
pathways <- list(
  Pathway_A = paste0("Gene", 1:10),
  Pathway_B = paste0("Gene", 11:20),
  Pathway_C = paste0("Gene", 21:30)
)
```

The `group` argument is the per-cell group label vector that accompanies the
screening results. It must have one entry per cell. The remaining arguments are
split automatically: arguments named like `FindMarkers()` formals go to
`FindMarkers()`, and arguments named like `fgsea()` formals go to `fgsea()`.

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-run
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
res <- BenchGSEA(
  sc,
  group = sc$truth,
  pathway = pathways,
  minSize = 5L,
  maxSize = 50L,
  nproc = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-table
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
res[, c("screenMethod", "pathway", "pval", "padj", "ES", "NES", "size"), with = FALSE]
```

The expected pattern is visible in the result: `Scissor` shows a positive
`NES` for `Pathway_A` and `scPAS` for `Pathway_B`, while `Pathway_C` is not
strongly enriched for either method. The enriched direction is given by the
sign of `NES`: a positive `NES` means the pathway is up in `"Positive"` cells,
a negative `NES` means it is down.

The tiny example produces tied ranking statistics, so `fgsea()` warns that the
order of tied genes is arbitrary. The warning is harmless here; on real data,
ties usually indicate that many markers share the same adjusted p-value and are
worth a quick look.

`leadingEdge` and `leadingEdgeStats` are list columns. They contain the genes
that drive each enrichment call and their ranking statistics, which is useful
for inspecting a pathway rather than only looking at its p-value:

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-leading
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
first_hit <- res[which.min(res$padj)]

first_hit$pathway
first_hit$leadingEdge[[1L]]
first_hit$leadingEdgeStats[[1L]]
```

# Input classes

`BenchGSEA()` dispatches on its input:

* a `Seurat` object is screened from its `meta.data` columns, as shown above;
* a `ScreenMethodResult` is unwrapped to its `scRNA_data` slot;
* a `BenchGSEAConfig` runs its configured screening methods first and then
  performs the GSEA comparison on the resulting object.

The configuration classes collect the shared inputs (`matched_bulk`,
`sc_data`, `phenotype`, `label_type`, `phenotype_class`, `screen_method` and
`method_param`) plus the GSEA-specific settings stored in `bench_config`. See
`?BenchGSEAConfig` and `?BenchGSEAConfigSet` for the complete constructor
interface and its validation rules.

# Running the screens inside the benchmark

If the screening has not been run yet, `BenchGSEAConfig()` can screen the data
first and then hand the resulting object to the GSEA comparison. `pathway`,
`group` and any `fgsea()` controls are collected by `BenchGSEAConfigSet()`:

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-config
#| eval: false
config <- BenchGSEAConfig(
  matched_bulk = bulk,
  sc_data = sc,
  phenotype = phenotype,
  label_type = "{method_name}",
  phenotype_class = "binary",
  screen_method = c("Scissor", "scPAS"),
  method_param = MethodParamSet(
    Scissor_param = list(alpha = 0.05),
    scPAS_param = list(alpha = 0.01)
  ),
  bench_config = BenchGSEAConfigSet(
    sc_data = sc,
    pathway = pathways,
    group = sc$truth,
    minSize = 5L,
    maxSize = 50L
  )
)

res_cfg <- BenchGSEA(config, verbose = FALSE)
```

The same configuration can be reused to compare different pathway
collections: only `bench_config$pathway` needs to be replaced, while the
screening results are recomputed by `BenchGSEA()` for each call.

# Filtering markers

By default all markers returned by `FindMarkers()` are used. Supplying a
non-`NULL` `p_value_threshold` keeps only markers with adjusted p-value below
0.05 before ranking:

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-filter
#| eval: false
res_filtered <- BenchGSEA(
  sc,
  group = sc$truth,
  pathway = pathways,
  p_value_threshold = 0.05,
  minSize = 5L,
  maxSize = 50L
)
```

This is useful when a method returns many weak markers. Be aware that filtering
too aggressively can remove the signal of small pathways.

# Reading the result

The returned object has one row per method and pathway. The most useful columns
are:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `screenMethod` | Screening method that produced the labels |
| `pathway` | Gene set name from `pathway` |
| `pval`, `padj` | Enrichment p-value and its multiple-testing adjustment |
| `ES`, `NES` | Enrichment score and normalised enrichment score |
| `size` | Number of pathway genes present in the ranked list |
| `leadingEdge` | Genes driving the enrichment |
| `leadingEdgeStats` | Ranking statistic of each leading-edge gene |

A compact comparison across methods can be built with base R or `data.table`:

```{r}
#| label: benchgsea-summary
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
res_df <- as.data.frame(res)

aggregate(
  cbind(padj, NES) ~ screenMethod,
  data = res_df,
  FUN = function(x) round(mean(x), 3)
)
```

# Practical notes

* **Gene identifiers must match.** The pathway gene sets and the row names of
  the assay must use the same identifier space (for example, both gene
  symbols). Convert the object or the pathways first if they do not.
* **Pathway size matters.** `fgsea()` drops pathways outside `minSize` and
  `maxSize`. For a small demonstration dataset, lower these values; for real
  data, keep the defaults or tune them to the pathway collection.
* **Direction is relative to `"Positive"`.** `FindMarkers()` is always run with
  `ident.1 = "Positive"` and `ident.2 = "Other"`, so a positive `NES` means
  enrichment in the cells selected by the screening method.
* **This is a functional comparison, not an accuracy score.** A method can
  recover a biologically coherent program that is not the pathway you expected.
  Read `BenchGSEA()` together with `BenchAcc()` when a ground truth is
  available.
* **Reserved arguments.** `ident.1`, `ident.2` and `group.by` are managed by
  `BenchGSEA()` and must not be supplied in `...`.

# See also

* `BenchAcc()` for binary classification metrics against a ground truth.
* `BenchGeneScore()` for cell-level pathway scores.
* `BenchMemory()` for run time and memory.
* `fgsea::fgsea()` and `Seurat::FindMarkers()` for the underlying methods.
